title: Amazon Says AWS Can Hit $1 Trillion as AI Spending Tops $220B
dek: AWS sales jumped 39% in Q3, but investors balked at the AI price tag.
caption:
No company has ever made $1 trillion in annual revenue. Amazon thinks AWS can get there 🚀

In its Q3 results, Amazon said AWS sales jumped 39% to $46.0 billion, with operating income up to $17.8 billion. CEO Andy Jassy said AWS could grow over 40% in 2027 and 2028 and become a trillion-dollar revenue business within five to 10 years, calling enterprise AI adoption "very early days."

The catch is the cost. Amazon still expects about $220 billion in capital spending on AI infrastructure in 2026, and more in 2027. Free cash flow swung to a $42.4 billion outflow, and shares fell about 6% after hours.

At AI Parabellum we see this as the cloud industry's biggest bet yet. The chatbots and coding assistants you use run on this capacity, but remember a trillion-dollar goal is a forecast, not a result.

$42.4 billion out the door in a year. That's the free cash flow outflow behind Amazon's AI build-out, even as AWS grew 39% to $46.0 billion last quarter.

Andy Jassy says the spending will "forever change the size of Amazon." Wall Street wasn't convinced yet, sending shares down about 6%.
